definition: Oversight exercised by affected communities and democratic institutions rather than by technical experts or industry self-regulation. Emphasizes public accountability, community input, and democratic legitimacy in AI governance.
rationale_for_coinage: Skeptics insist that oversight must be democratic and participatory — not delegated to the same experts and corporations building AI. Safetyists default to expert-led technical oversight; accelerationists prefer market-driven or audit-based oversight. The bare term conceals who exercises oversight and on whose behalf.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Human control oversight is about technical ability to intervene in AI systems; democratic oversight is about who has legitimate authority to govern AI.
Audit oversight is about empirical verification by experts; democratic oversight is about community and public institutional authority.

contested_aspects: Whether democratic institutions can move fast enough to oversee rapidly evolving AI
How to ensure meaningful participation vs. performative consultation
